_about: State auto-IRA programs (lexflow.benefits.programs). Every fact cites a verbatim quote matched by lexflow's software.

programs.name: CalSavers Retirement Savings Program

facts.text: California created the CalSavers Retirement Savings Program under the CalSavers Retirement Savings Trust Act.

sources.quote: “CalSavers Retirement Savings Program” or “program” means a retirement savings program offered pursuant to the CalSavers Retirement Savings Trust Act.

facts.text: A nine-member CalSavers Retirement Savings Board, chaired by the State Treasurer, runs the program.

sources.quote: There is hereby created within state government the CalSavers Retirement Savings Board, which shall consist of nine members, with the Treasurer serving as chair, as follows:

facts.text: Eligible employers that do not offer a retirement plan must offer CalSavers through payroll deduction or certify an exemption; since January 1, 2026 this covers employers with one or more employees.

sources.quote: By December 31, 2025, eligible employers with one or more eligible employees and that do not offer a retirement savings program pursuant to subdivision (h) shall have a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the program.
Effective January 1, 2026, all California employers with one or more employees are required by law to provide access to a qualified retirement program or certify a valid exemption with CalSavers.

facts.text: Employers with more than 100 eligible employees: within 12 months after the program opened for enrollment.

sources.quote: Within 12 months after the board opens the program for enrollment, eligible employers with more than 100 eligible employees and that do not offer a retirement savings program pursuant to subdivision (h) shall have a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the program.

facts.text: Employers with more than 50 eligible employees: within 24 months after opening (the program page gave June 30, 2021).

sources.quote: Within 24 months after the board opens the program for enrollment, eligible employers with more than 50 eligible employees and that do not offer a retirement savings program pursuant to subdivision (h) shall have a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the program.
If you have more than 50 employees and don't sponsor a plan, you must register with CalSavers by June 30, 2021.

facts.text: Employers with 5 or more employees: within 36 months after the program opened for enrollment.

sources.quote: Within 36 months after the board opens the program for enrollment, eligible employers with five or more employees and that do not offer a retirement savings program pursuant to subdivision (h) shall have a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the program.

facts.text: Employers with 1 or more eligible employees: by December 31, 2025.

sources.quote: By December 31, 2025, eligible employers with one or more eligible employees and that do not offer a retirement savings program pursuant to subdivision (h) shall have a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the program.
Eligible employers with at least one employee in 2024 are required to register unless they meet one of the conditions for exemption

facts.text: Employers offering a tax-qualified plan (such as a 401(k), SEP, SIMPLE or defined benefit plan) or an automatic-enrollment payroll IRA are exempt; government employers and businesses with no employees other than the owners are not eligible employers.

sources.quote: An employer that provides an employer-sponsored retirement plan, such as a defined benefit plan or a 401(k), Simplified Employee Pension (SEP) plan, or Savings Incentive Match Plan for Employees (SIMPLE) plan, or that offers an automatic enrollment payroll deduction IRA, shall be exempt from the requirements of the CalSavers Retirement Savings Program

excluding sole proprietorships, self-employed individuals, or other business entities that do not employ any individuals other than the owners of the business, the federal government, the state, any county, any municipal corporation, or any of the state’s units or instrumentalities,

facts.text: Self-employed individuals are not mandated employers but may save in CalSavers on their own.

sources.quote: CalSavers is available to California workers whose employers don’t offer a retirement plan, self-employed individuals, and others who want to save extra.

facts.text: $250 per eligible employee after a final notice, plus $500 per eligible employee if noncompliance continues.

sources.quote: shall be subject to a penalty of two hundred fifty dollars ($250) per eligible employee and an additional penalty of five hundred dollars ($500) per eligible employee if noncompliance continues as described in Section 19287 of the Revenue and Taxation Code.

facts.text: The statute sets a 3% default and lets the board set it by regulation anywhere from 2% to 5%.

sources.quote: Unless otherwise specified by the employee, a participating employee shall contribute 3 percent of the employee’s annual salary or wages to the program.

By regulation, the board may adjust the contribution amount set in subdivision (j) to no less than 2 percent and no more than 5 percent and may vary that amount within that 2 percent to 5 percent range.

programs.notes: The statute leaves the first three waves' dates relative to the program's opening; only the 51+ wave date (June 30, 2021) is stated on an official page that was read (saver.calsavers.com, a stale banner), so the 101+ and 5+ waves carry no deadline. The board's current default rate (widely reported as 5%) is not quoted from a page here, so the default fact shows the statutory 3% and the 2-5% range.

programs.name: Colorado SecureSavings

facts.text: Colorado SecureSavings was created by state law.

sources.quote: Here in Colorado, nearly 940,000 workers have no employer-sponsored retirement savings plan. Colorado SecureSavings was created by law to meet this urgent need.
Colorado SecureSavings is a new retirement savings program, created by the State of Colorado.

facts.text: A state board (called the Colorado Secure Savings Plan Board in the 2020 study reports on the Treasury page) oversees the program.

sources.quote: The Fiscal Impacts of Insufficient Retirement Savings in Colorado: a report to the Colorado Secure Savings Plan Board, February 2020.

facts.text: Eligible employers must register or certify an exemption by their deadline.

sources.quote: All eligible employers must register or certify their exemption by the deadline

facts.text: Employers with 5 or more employees, in business at least 2 years, without a qualified plan.

sources.quote: Colorado employers are required to facilitate the program if they: Have been in business for at least 2 years Have 5 or more employees, and Don’t offer a qualified retirement plan

facts.text: Registration deadline shown for new businesses: May 15, 2025; deadlines for existing businesses have passed.

sources.quote: New businesses Registration May 15, 2025 deadline Existing Colorado businesses Your registration deadline has passed

facts.text: Employers with a qualified plan, fewer than 2 years in business, or fewer than 5 employees certify an exemption.

sources.quote: Employers who provide a qualified retirement plan to their employees, have been in business for less than 2 years, or have fewer than 5 employees should certify their exemption from the program using their provided Access Code.

facts.text: Self-employed individuals may join on their own.

sources.quote: Colorado SecureSavings is also available for: Colorado workers whose employers do not offer a workplace retirement plan Self-employed individuals

facts.text: 5% of gross pay, rising 1 point a year to 8% unless the saver chooses otherwise.

sources.quote: The default savings rate for a Colorado SecureSavings account is 5% of your gross pay, and that amount is deducted from your paycheck after taxes have been taken out.
Your contribution rate will automatically increase by one percentage point each year until it reaches 8% of your total pay (wages before taxes and other deductions), unless you choose otherwise.

programs.notes: This copy of lexflow has no Colorado statute index, so the program rests on official pages alone (coloradosecuresavings.com via Internet Archive captures, and the State Treasury page via a 2025 capture). No penalty is recorded: none was stated on the pages read. The board's name is grounded only by a 2020 report title on the Treasury page.

programs.name: MyCTSavings (Connecticut Retirement Security Program)
programs.board: Connecticut Retirement Security Advisory Board (program run by the State Comptroller)

facts.text: State law establishes the Connecticut Retirement Security Program, offered as MyCTSavings and overseen by the State Comptroller.

sources.quote: “Program” means the Connecticut Retirement Security Program established pursuant to section 31-418
MyCTSavings is overseen by the Connecticut Office of the State Comptroller.

facts.text: The Connecticut Retirement Security Advisory Board advises; the Comptroller administers the program.

sources.quote: “Board” means the Connecticut Retirement Security Advisory Board established pursuant to section 31-417

facts.text: Qualified employers without a retirement plan must automatically enroll covered employees, who may opt out.

sources.quote: such qualified employer shall automatically enroll each of its covered employees in the program at the participant's contribution level in accordance with the provisions of section 31-71j
Eligible Connecticut businesses are required to facilitate MyCTSavings if they don’t offer a retirement plan

facts.text: Employers with 5 or more employees in Connecticut (on October 1 of the prior year, at least five paid $5,000 or more).

sources.quote: “Qualified employer” means any person, corporation, limited liability company, firm, partnership, voluntary association, joint stock association or other entity doing business in the state during the calendar year, whether for profit or not for profit, that employed on October first of the preceding calendar year five or more individuals in the state
State law requires that all businesses with 5 or more employees that do not already offer a qualified retirement plan register before their required deadline.

facts.text: Registration deadline shown for newly eligible businesses: August 31, 2025 (earlier waves have passed).

sources.quote: Newly eligible businesses August 31, 2025 Next deadline Businesses previously notified Your registration deadline has passed

facts.text: Employers that maintain a qualified plan or another arrangement the Comptroller approves are exempt and certify the exemption.

sources.quote: or (ii) any other retirement arrangement approved by the Comptroller, shall be exempt from the requirements of subdivisions (1) and (2) of this subsection.
Employers who provide a qualified retirement plan to their employees should certify their exemption from the program using their provided Access Code.

facts.text: Self-employed individuals may join on their own.

sources.quote: MyCTSavings is also available for: Connecticut workers whose employers do not offer a workplace retirement plan Self-employed individuals

facts.text: No per-employee fine is set; an employee, the Labor Commissioner or the Comptroller may sue to compel enrollment.

sources.quote: If a qualified employer fails to enroll a covered employee as required under subsection (a) of section 31-422 , such covered employee, the Labor Commissioner or the Comptroller, may bring a civil action to require the qualified employer to enroll the covered employee

facts.text: The program default is 5% of gross pay; the statute's fallback contribution level is 3% of taxable wages.

sources.quote: The default savings rate for a MyCTSavings account is 5% of your gross pay (the amount you earn before taxes)
in the absence of an affirmative election by the participant, three per cent of the participant's taxable wages

programs.notes: myctsavings.com refuses automated readers; its pages were read from Internet Archive captures (2026). The statute's 3% fallback and the program page's 5% default differ; the page reflects the current program setting. Hawaii's board voted in February 2026 to join the MyCT partnership (see the Hawaii entry).

programs.name: Delaware EARNS (Expanding Access for Retirement and Necessary Saving)

facts.text: Delaware established the EARNS Program, a state-facilitated retirement savings program.

sources.quote: There is hereby established the Expanding Access for Retirement and Necessary Saving (“EARNS”) Program to serve as a vehicle through which covered employees may, on a voluntary basis, provide for additional retirement security through a state-facilitated retirement saving program

facts.text: The Delaware EARNS Program Board governs the program.

sources.quote: “Board” means the Delaware EARNS Program Board established under § 3803 of this title.
EARNS is governed by the EARNS Program Board (“EPB”), an instrumentality of the State of Delaware.

facts.text: Covered employers must register with EARNS and offer it to covered employees, or certify an exemption.

sources.quote: When and as required by the Board, covered employers shall: a. Register with the Program and provide the program administrator relevant information about the employer’s employees.
All eligible employers must register or certify their exemption by the deadline

facts.text: Employers with 5 or more covered employees (now and in the prior year) in business in Delaware at least 6 months of the prior year.

sources.quote: including a nonprofit entity, that employs, and during the previous calendar year employed, at least 5 covered employees, and that has been in business in this State for at least 6 months in the immediately preceding calendar year.
Program eligibility You’re required to register if you: Have 5 or more employees* Have been in business since July 1 of the previous year Do not offer qualified retirement plan

facts.text: Next registration deadline shown for newly eligible businesses: June 30, 2026.

sources.quote: Newly eligible businesses June 30, 2026 NEXT deadline Businesses notified before January 1, 2026 Your registration deadline has passed

facts.text: Employers with a qualified plan or fewer than 5 employees certify an exemption.

sources.quote: Employers who provide a qualified retirement plan to their employees or have fewer than 5 employees should certify their exemption from the program using their provided Access Code.

facts.text: Self-employed individuals may join on their own.

sources.quote: EARNS is available for: Delaware workers whose employers do not offer a workplace retirement plan Self-employed individuals

facts.text: Administrative penalties up to $250 per employee per year, capped at $5,000 per year.

sources.quote: The Board may, in a final order, impose administrative penalties against a covered employer who fails to comply with this chapter or any regulation promulgated under this chapter, which penalties shall not exceed $250 per employee per year, up to a maximum total penalty of $5,000 per year.

facts.text: 5% of gross pay unless the saver chooses otherwise; the board may set the default between 3% and 6%.

sources.quote: The default savings rate for an EARNS account is 5% of your gross pay, and that amount is deducted from your paycheck after taxes have been taken out.
It shall not be less than 3% nor more than 6% of compensation.

programs.notes: earnsdelaware.com refuses automated readers; its pages were read from Internet Archive captures (2026).

programs.name: Hawaiʻi Retirement Savings Program (HRSP)

facts.text: Hawaii has a state-sponsored retirement savings program for private-sector employees without a workplace plan; it has not launched yet.

sources.quote: Welcome to the Hawaiʻi Retirement Savings Program (HRSP), a state-sponsored retirement savings plan designed for private-sector employees who don’t have access to an employer-sponsored retirement plan.

facts.text: The Hawaii Retirement Savings Board is finalizing the implementation plan.

sources.quote: The Hawaii Retirement Savings Board is finalizing the implementation plan, and we will update this page with the next steps as soon as they are available.

facts.text: Private-sector employers with at least one employee must facilitate HRSP or offer a qualifying plan; 2025 legislation switched the program to automatic enrollment.

sources.quote: If you are a private-sector employer in Hawaii with at least one employee, you must either: Enroll in and facilitate the state-run HRSP program. Offer your employee(s) a qualifying retirement plan, such as a 401(k).
Automatic enrollment (Effective May 29, 2025): Recent legislation changed the program to an automatic enrollment model.

facts.text: Employers with 1 or more employees (once the program is active).

sources.quote: If you are a private-sector employer in Hawaii with at least one employee, you must either: Enroll in and facilitate the state-run HRSP program. Offer your employee(s) a qualifying retirement plan, such as a 401(k).

facts.text: Projected program launch: late December 2026.

sources.quote: The Hawaiʻi Retirement Savings Program is projected to launch in late December 2026, provided there are no extenuating circumstances.

facts.text: Employers that already offer a qualified retirement plan are exempt.

sources.quote: Exemption for existing plans: If you already offer a qualified retirement plan to your employees, you are exempt from the program.

facts.text: Once the program is active, noncompliant employers may face penalties of up to $5,000 per calendar year.

sources.quote: required to participate and fail to do so once the program is active, you may face penalties. These penalties could be up to $5,000 per calendar year.

facts.text: 5% of compensation unless the saver chooses otherwise.

sources.quote: Default contribution rate: The default contribution rate is set at 5% of your compensation.

programs.notes: Hawaii's program statute (HRS chapter 389) is not in this copy's statute index, so the entry rests on the Department of Labor and Industrial Relations' official HRSP pages (read live 2026-10-22). In February 2026 the board voted to join Connecticut's MyCT partnership.

programs.name: My Illinois Savings (formerly Illinois Secure Choice)

facts.text: The Illinois Secure Choice Savings Program Act created the state program, now branded My Illinois Savings.

sources.quote: The Illinois Secure Choice Savings Program Act [820 ILCS 80] establishes a state-facilitated retirement savings program, now known as My Illinois Savings, for private-sector workers in Illinois who lack access to a qualified employer-sponsored retirement plan.
My Illinois Savings, formerly known as Illinois Secure Choice, is a state-facilitated retirement savings program that provides Illinois workers with a simple way to save for the future.

facts.text: A seven-member Illinois Secure Choice Savings Board, chaired by the State Treasurer, governs the program.

sources.quote: There is created the Illinois Secure Choice Savings Board. (a) The Board shall consist of the following 7 members: (1) the State Treasurer, or his or her designee, who shall serve as chair;

facts.text: Covered employers must set up payroll deposit to the program on the Board's timeline unless they offer their own qualified plan.

sources.quote: Each employer shall establish a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow each employee to participate in the Program within the timeline set by the Board after the Program opens for enrollment.
State law now requires every Illinois employer with five or more employees to offer their own retirement program or facilitate Secure Choice.

facts.text: Employers with at least 5 Illinois employees in every quarter of the prior year and 2 or more years in business; the statute sets the 5-15 employee enrollment deadline no sooner than September 1, 2023.

sources.quote: "Employer" means a person or entity engaged in a business, industry, profession, trade, or other enterprise in Illinois, whether for profit or not for profit, that (i) has employed at least 5 employees in the State during every quarter of the previous calendar year, (ii) has been in business at least 2 years,
The enrollment deadline for employers with at least 5 employees but not more than 15 employees shall be no sooner than September 1, 2023.

Under Illinois law, businesses must participate in My Illinois Savings or offer a qualified retirement plan if they: Had at least five Illinois employees in every quarter of the previous calendar year Have been in business for two or more years

facts.text: Employers that offer or contribute to a qualified plan (401(k), 403(b), SEP, SIMPLE and similar) are not covered.

sources.quote: and (iii) is not offering or contributing to a qualified retirement plan, including, but not limited to, a plan qualified under Section 401(a), Section 401(k), Section 403(a), Section 403(b),

facts.text: Anyone, including self-employed people, may sign up on their own.

sources.quote: is also available to people who choose to sign up on their own, including self-employed individuals.

facts.text: $250 per employee for the first noncompliant calendar year and $500 per employee for each later noncompliant year.

sources.quote: shall be subject to a penalty equal to: (1) $250 per employee for the first calendar year the employer is noncompliant; or (2) $500 per employee for each subsequent calendar year the employer is noncompliant;

facts.text: 5% of pay into a target-date Roth IRA unless the saver chooses otherwise.

sources.quote: Workers who participate in My Illinois Savings are automatically enrolled in a default target-date Roth IRA with a default 5% payroll contribution.

programs.notes: The program was renamed My Illinois Savings (Treasurer's page, read live 2026-10-22); ilsecurechoice.com now redirects to myilsavings.com, which refuses automated readers, so the ilsecurechoice.com quote comes from a June 2026 archive capture. The statute gives only 'no sooner than' floors for the 16-24 and 5-15 waves; the Board's actual wave dates were not found on a readable page.

programs.name: Massachusetts CORE Plan (Connecting Organizations to Retirement)
programs.board: Office of the State Treasurer and Receiver General

facts.text: The Treasurer may sponsor a qualified defined contribution plan that small nonprofits can adopt.

sources.quote: The treasurer and receiver general, on behalf of the commonwealth, may sponsor a qualified defined contribution plan within the meaning of section 414(i) of the Internal Revenue Code,

facts.text: The State Treasurer's office sponsors the plan and handles most administration and investment.

sources.quote: The Office of the State Treasurer and Receiver General, as sponsor of the CORE Plan, assumes most administrative and investment responsibilities, reducing the burden on participating nonprofit employers.

facts.text: A voluntary 401(k) for Massachusetts nonprofits with 100 or fewer employees (the limit was 20 before July 1, 2025); employers choose to adopt it.

sources.quote: The Massachusetts Defined Contribution CORE Plan (“CORE Plan”) is a tax deferred and post-tax 401(k) savings plan developed for employees of eligible small nonprofit organizations that choose to adopt it.
Massachusetts nonprofit organizations with 100 employees or fewer may be eligible to adopt the CORE Plan.
doing business in the commonwealth and employing not more than 100 persons, but shall not include a governmental employer.

programs.notes: A voluntary 401(k) for nonprofits, not an auto-IRA.

programs.name: MarylandSaves (the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program)
programs.board: Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board

facts.text: Maryland law creates the Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program, made of payroll deposit IRA arrangements chosen by the Board (MarylandSaves).

sources.quote: The Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Program shall only include one or more payroll deposit IRA arrangements as determined by the Board.
Maryland’s retirement and emergency savings program designed for small businesses and those who make them

facts.text: The Maryland Small Business Retirement Savings Board, an instrumentality of the State, runs the program.

sources.quote: The Board is a body politic and corporate and is an instrumentality of the State.

facts.text: Covered employers must set up a payroll deposit arrangement and automatically enrol covered employees unless they opt out; an employer may instead offer its own plan at any time.

sources.quote: After the Board opens the Program for enrollment, covered employers shall establish a payroll deposit retirement savings arrangement to allow employee participation in the Program.

facts.text: A covered employer is any private employer in Maryland, for profit or not, that pays its employees through a payroll system or service and has been in business during the current and preceding calendar year; there is no headcount floor.

sources.quote: “Covered employer” means a person engaged in a business, an industry, a profession, a trade, or any other enterprise in the State, whether for profit or not for profit, that pays the covered employer’s employees through a payroll system or service.

facts.text: Governments, employers offering (or having offered in the preceding two calendar years) their own savings arrangement, and employers not in business throughout the current and preceding year are not covered.

Note: Your business must also be in good standing with SDAT to receive the fee waiver.
